newsitem.title: USA: More new hotels planned for Philadelphia -- paper.
newsitem.headline: More new hotels planned for Philadelphia -- paper.

text.p: A new round of announcements heralding new hotels for Philadelphia means the city's hotel room count will jump to 9,000 from 7,600 in the next several years, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Friday.
Mayor Ed Rendell said the expansions would mean Philadelphia could now compete for a national political convention.
The mayor detailed plans for a $105 million hotel run by Loews Hotels, to open in early 1999, and said another hotel, with 1,200 rooms, would open near Philadelphia International Airport.

City officials have heard "expressions of interest" from numerous other developers as well, as the city's hotel boom continues, the newspaper said. The expansions also mean the city can expect more business from large conventions reluctant to come to Philadelphia because of a lack of hotel rooms.
